note: Collision dials (TASKS 'collision dial'), as reported by qb6 per level; scripts/results/build.mjs reads this into results.json (collisionDials) and RESULTS.md. Update after each level.

comment.label: measured on Cloudflare: 1,000 agents (20 copies of VS Code extensions/ x 50), cached answers (no model call), one declaration-level comment task at a time, claims off unless marked "+ claims" (an agent claims its declarations before reading the file); collisions = pairs of tasks started at the same moment

levels.lostNote: 20 = one file per copy with '} export class X' on one line: comment placed above the '}' (a doc.js targeting bug from F3 on, fixed in 6807d72), not a collision
levels.landNote: landing times not comparable: the Lander stalled on Artifacts internal errors until trees were memoised mid-level

levels.lostNote: the same 20 targeting-bug files as dial 0, none from collisions
15 = an accounting artefact: the fixed agent correctly skips the one-line '} export class' declaration, but the record still listed it as intended (records keep only inserted comments from L60 on)
9 = the same accounting artefact as L30 (these agents ran before the record fix deployed); not lost work
11 = the same accounting artefact; 1 task left 'ready' (not landed), being looked at

comment.caveat: In cached mode the second comment of a same-declaration pair is derived from the first (its first sentence, or that plus a stock phrase), so 'duplicate, kept the first' says which landed first, not which answer was better. Which version wins under real collisions is measured by the code dial, where the hidden tests decide.
comment.finding: Across dial 0-60% (1,000 agents) throughput stayed ~1,100-1,280 tasks/s and land wait p50 ~96-114 s; 0 doubled comments, 0 code changes, nothing lost at any level. Same-declaration collisions resolve at landing ('duplicate, kept the first', or a replay when the declaration is still undocumented) or, with claims on, before any work: at 60% + claims all 8,424 second-of-pair tasks were caught early and 0 duplicates reached the Lander, at ~9% higher throughput (1,276 vs 1,167 tasks/s).

code.label: measured on Cloudflare: kata (sim/kata/seed-1, hidden tests in lab-hidden), 1,385 tasks per level, 200 fleet agents (Gemini 3.1 flash-lite, glm-4.7 overflow), every change through qodebase's real merge queue (trains of 8, bounces, model replays); checked on main by lab-hidden/kata/check.mjs --attribute (each lost requirement replayed on the commit where it landed)

levels.note: At dial 0 the losses are model mistakes: 76 of 96 were already wrong in the commit where they landed, 19 were dropped by a later agent that read main with the requirement in; 1 lost in landing (a redo that started before the requirement landed; the redo's start time is approximate). 54 rejected = a harness bug (stale fork read; fixed 16:38), 22 cut by deploys.
